sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r5/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row #7 'task_asks_for_a_real_working_product' and Internal Quality Checks row #7 (no extra annotation text in the row)
evidence: The brief demands a full-stack, multi-user product built from an empty /app (environment/Dockerfile creates /app with only .gitkeep; the template server.js stub is not shipped to the agent): Express+SQLite server at /app/server.js with seed import, persistence across restarts and DB_PATH (integration.md), five-account sign-in with role/client scoping, airtight ethical walls across list/thread/search/snippets/quotes/unread/mentions/links/transcripts plus live wall changes (walls-and-retention.md), disappearing-message timers against a fixed clock, legal holds, edit history with stale-edit refusal, 3-level nested replies, safe formatting, message links, @-mention suggestions, per-user unread lines, idempotent sends, ~5 s live updates and a transcript page (conversations.md). The golden is ~1.5k lines (server.js 527, app.js 654). Smallest-submission test: a static page/mock fails both gates - render (gates/render/judge.toml) requires real sign-in with seeded matters and wrong-password rejection, and constraints (gates/constraints/judge.toml) requires a post that survives reload and is visible to harriet in a separate browser context; functional/prompt.md also zeroes a 'static mock, static shell, missing backend, or seeded-looking facade'. A single CRUD screen passes gates but then needs functional > 0.05 (scoring.toml [floors], score.py:47-48), i.e. >2.1 of 42 weight; every functional criterion is binary and conjunctive with positive controls and server-side replays (e.g. nested_replies needs 3-level nesting with parent quotes ordered under parent; sent_once_in_order needs replay dedupe plus stable same-timestamp order across thread/search/transcript), so a trivial CRUD screen earns 0 and reward 0. Weak-app probe: the cheapest positive-reward app I could construct is a generic threaded chat without walls/timers/holds (nested_replies 1.5 + safe_formatting 1.5 + sent_once_in_order 2.5 = 5.5/42 = 0.13 > floor) plus polish/visual craft, estimated ~0.3-0.4 reward; that is still real build work (auth, persistence, threading, search, transcript, idempotency), not a stub or trivial tweak, so row 7 is satisfied; whether that partial credit is too generous for omitting the brief's two top priorities is a reward-shaping question for other rows. Conforming-alternative probe: nothing in the brief or criteria requires a specific route, framework or layout (functional/prompt.md: 'Any endpoint path, payload shape or cookie name is acceptable'), so a different real build is not penalised on row-7 grounds. Risk=true because raw-evidence-index.json states reward discrimination/ranking on these bytes is absent: no measured no-op/stub/weak-app run confirms the gates and floor zero a stub in the configured judge; the analysis above is source-based only.
